title: Rare Ball cabbage (Rareball repolyo): Characteristics
metaDescription: Rare Ball cabbage is an imported variety (Japan) cabbage variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Rare Ball cabbage is an imported variety (Japan) cabbage variety, also sold or known as Rareball repolyo. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Kaneko Seeds (Japan).

heroImage.alt: Vegetable terraces and plastic tunnels on the slopes of Mankayan, Benguet, the kind of farm where Rare Ball cabbage is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Rareball repolyo, this is the same cabbage. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cabbage variety finder](/crop-varieties/cabbage), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cabbage fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 24 t/ha marketable, averaged over three Benguet sites and four seasons under organic growing (BSU trial).
**Fruit:** Head: round, green and compact, the heaviest heads in the BSU trial, about 520 g on average under organic growing.
**Season:** Dry and wet seasons in the highlands.
Out yielded Scorpio in several of the BSU trial seasons.
Low share of non marketable heads in the dry season at high elevation (BSU).

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: top marketable yield in the Benguet State University organic cabbage trial, which recommends it with Lucky Ball and Scorpio for Benguet, also listed in DA's cabbage production guide. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Rare Ball cabbage

Most repolyo comes from the highlands, where it heads well. Lowland growers need a heat tolerant hybrid and a cool month. Pick a firm head that keeps on the trip to market. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Rareball repolyo the same as Rare Ball?
items.a: Yes. Rareball repolyo is another name for Rare Ball. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Rare Ball?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
